story: The stock went up. Why did your call lose money?

segments.label: MONEY LAB
segments.title: Stock up 4%. Your call down.
segments.narration: The stock went up four percent. Your call option still lost money. Here is why.

segments.label: THE SETUP
segments.title: Bought a $105 call for $2.48
segments.narration: Before earnings, the stock is at one hundred dollars. A one-oh-five call with a week left costs 2.48 dollars, because implied volatility is eighty percent.

segments.label: AFTER EARNINGS
segments.title: Stock $104. Call $1.18.
segments.narration: Earnings land. The stock rises to one oh four. But volatility collapses to thirty percent, and the call is now worth 1.18. Down 52 percent.

segments.label: THE CHART
segments.title: Breakeven: stock at $106.50
segments.narration: After the crush, the stock needs to reach about 106.50 dollars just to get your money back.

segments.label: THE LESSON
segments.title: You paid for the expected move
segments.narration: Before earnings, option prices already include a big expected move. If the real move is smaller, you lose, even if you guessed the direction.

segments.label: AUGASTER MONEY LAB
segments.title: The math behind money
segments.narration: Education only, not advice. Follow for more Money Lab.
